div.head: Af 40
div.ab: Cyninges burgbryce bið CXX scill., ærcebiscepes hundnigontig scill., oðres biscepes ⁊ ealdormonnes LX scill., twelfhyndes monnes XXX scill., syxhyndes monnes XV scill.; ceorles edorbryce V scill.
Cyninges burhbrice bið CXX scll', ercebiscopes XC scll', oðres biscopes ⁊ ealdermonnes LX scll', XIIhyndes monnes XXX scll', syxhyndes monnes XV scll'; ceorles edorbrice V scll'.

Be burhbryce. Cyninges burhbryce bið hundtwelftig scill', ercebisceopes hundnigonti scill', oþres bisceopes ⁊ ealdormannes syxtig scill', twelfhyndes mannes ðrittig scill', syxhyndes mannes fiftene scyll'. [Ceorles eoderbryce fif scill'.]
… hundnigontig s …, oþres bisceopes ⁊ ealdorm … LX scill', twelf . . ndes monnes XXX scill', syx … XV scill', ceorles edorbryce … . ll'.

Regis burhbrece est hundtwelfti (CXX) sol., archiepiscopi hundnigontig scillinga (XC sol)., episcopi et aldermanni (quem Latine comitem uel seniorem dicunt) LX sol.; twelfhindes hominis XXX sol., sexhyndi hominis XV sol.; ceorli ederbrece (id est rustici sepis fractio) V sol. (emendetur).

[Be burhbryce.] Cyninges burgbryce bið CXX scill., ærcebiscepes hundnigontig scill., oðres biscepes ⁊ ealdormonnes LX scill., twelfhyndes monnes XXX scill., syxhyndes monnes XV scill.; ceorles edorbryce V scill.
Cyninges burgbryce bið CXX scill, ærcebiscepes hundnigontig scill, oðres biscepes ⁊ ealdormonnes LX scill, twelfhyndes monnes XXX scill, syxhyndes monnes XV scill, ceorles edorbryce V scill.

[Die Busse für] Eindringen in die Burg [das feste Haus] des Königs ist 120 Schill.; des Erzbischofs 90 Schill.; eines anderen Bischofs und eines Ealdorman 60 Schill., eines 1200-[Schilling-]Mannes 30 Schill., eines 600-[Schilling-]Mannes 15 Schill.; [die Busse für] Eindringen in den Zaun eines Gemeinfreien: 5 Schill.

[The compensation for] breaking into the fortress [fortified house] of the king is 120 shillings; of the archbishop, 90 shillings; of another bishop and of an ealdorman, 60 shillings; of a 1200-[shilling] man, 30 shillings; of a 600-[shilling] man, 15 shillings; [the compensation for] breaking through a common freeman’s fence: 5 shillings.

The fine for breaking into the fortified premises of the king shall be 120 shillings; into those of an archbishop, 90 shillings; into those of another bishop or of an ealdorman, 60 shillings; into those of a man whose wergeld is 1200 shillings, 30 shillings; into those of a man whose wergeld is 600 shillings, 15 shillings. The fine for breaking through a commoner’s fence shall be 5 shillings.

Forcible entry into the king’s residence shall be 120 shillings; into the archbishop’s, 90 shillings; into another bishop’s or an ealdorman’s, 60 shillings; into that of a man of a twelve-hundred wergild, 30 shillings; into that of a man of a six-hundred wergild, 15 shillings; forcible entry into a ceorl’s enclosure, five shillings.

[The fine for] breaking into the king’s fortified dwelling is 120 shillings; an archbishop’s 90; another [lesser] bishop’s or an ealdorman’s 60 shillings; a man [whose wer is] 1,200 [shillings], 30 shillings; a man [whose wer is] 600 [shillings], 15 shillings; breaking into a ceorl’s enclosure 5 shillings.

note.quote: there were a significant number of cases where Alfred contradicted Ine. Ine, for example, set the 'burhbryce' ... (n. 8: Ine 45, Af. 40)

note.label: reforms
note.quote: others positively 'reformed' Ine's decrees (as on burhbryce) (n. 78: Af 40/Ine 45 (burhbryce))

note.label: cf. (wergeld enumerations)

note.label: emends
note.quote: Ine §45 sets the fine for breaking into the fortified dwelling of a king or bishop at 120 shillings. Alfred §41 emends this

Der Bruch des Hausfriedens (s. d. Gl 2a. 3) durch rechtlich ins Haus Gelangte kostet etwas mehr. — Vgl. Gl Einbruch 2d
Breach of the peace of the house (see that word in Gl 2a. 3) by persons who have lawfully come into the house costs somewhat more. — Cf. Gl Einbruch 2d
nicht ‘Stadt’. Im Ggs. zum Bauernhause, das ein blosser Zaun schützt, ist die burh umfestigt, wohl mit Wall und Graben; Maitland Domesday 184. Vgl. Gl Burg 1. a; Burgtor 1—c
not ‘town’. In contrast to the peasant’s house, which a mere fence protects, the burh is fortified all round, probably with rampart and ditch; Maitland Domesday 184. Cf. Gl Burg 1. a; Burgtor 1—c
